descriptions.value: OpenSSH, when using OPIE (One-Time Passwords in Everything) for PAM, allows remote attackers to determine the existence of certain user accounts, which displays a different response if the user account exists and is configured to use one-time passwords (OTP), a similar issue to CVE-2007-2243.

OpenSSH, cuando utiliza OPIE(One-Time Passwords in Everything) para PAM, permiet a atacantes remotos determinar la existencia de ciertas cuentas de usuarios, lo cual muestra una respuesta diferente si la cuenta de usuario existe y si está configurada para utilizar one-time passwords (OTP), un asunto similar es el CVE-2007-2243.

vendorComments.comment: Not vulnerable. OPIE for PAM is not shipped with Red Hat Enterprise Linux 2.1, 3, 4, or 5.

descriptions.value: Certain Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) 4 and 5 packages for OpenSSH, as signed in August 2008 using a legitimate Red Hat GPG key, contain an externally introduced modification (Trojan Horse) that allows the package authors to have an unknown impact.  NOTE: since the malicious packages were not distributed from any official Red Hat sources, the scope of this issue is restricted to users who may have obtained these packages through unofficial distribution points.  As of 20080827, no unofficial distributions of this software are known.

Ciertos paquetes Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) 4 y 5 para OpenSSH, como fueron firmados en agosto de 2008 usando una clave Red Hat GPG legítima, contienen una modificación introducida externamente (Trojan Horse) que permite a los autores de los paquetes tener un impacto desconocido. NOTA: como los paquetes maliciosos no fueron distribuidos por ninguna fuente Red Hat oficial, el impacto de este problema está restringido a usuarios que pudieran haber obtenido estos paquetes a través de puntos de distribución no oficiales. Como en 20080827, los distribuidores no oficiales de este software son conocidos.

cve.evaluatorComment:
This alert is primarily for those who may obtain Red Hat binary 
packages via channels other than those of official Red Hat subscribers.  Packages obtained by Red Hat Enterprise Linux subscribers via Red Hat Network are not at risk. 

Redhat has provided a shell script which lists the affected packages and can verify that none of them are installed on a system at the following location:

https://www.redhat.com/security/data/openssh-blacklist-1.0.sh

descriptions.value: OpenSSH through 10.0, when common types of DRAM are used, might allow row hammer attacks (for authentication bypass) because the integer value of authenticated in mm_answer_authpassword does not resist flips of a single bit. NOTE: this is applicable to a certain threat model of attacker-victim co-location in which the attacker has user privileges. NOTE: this is disputed by the Supplier, who states "we do not consider it to be the application's responsibility to defend against platform architectural weaknesses."

OpenSSH hasta 9.6, cuando se utilizan tipos comunes de DRAM, podría permitir row hammer attacks (para omitir la autenticación) porque el valor entero de autenticado en mm_answer_authpassword no resiste cambios de un solo bit. NOTA: esto es aplicable a un determinado modelo de amenaza de ubicación conjunta entre atacante y víctima en el que el atacante tiene privilegios de usuario.

affectedData.product: SIMATIC S7-1500 TM MFP - GNU/Linux subsystem

descriptions.value: sftp in OpenSSH before 10.4 does not properly constrain the location of downloaded files when "sftp server:/path ." is used with an attacker-controlled server.
sftp en OpenSSH antes de la 10.4 no restringe adecuadamente la ubicación de los archivos descargados cuando se utiliza ’sftp servidor:/ruta .’ con un servidor controlado por un atacante.
scp in OpenSSH before 10.4 may place a file in the parent directory of an intended directory when the copy occurs between two remote destinations.
scp en OpenSSH anterior a 10.4 puede colocar un archivo en el directorio padre de un directorio previsto cuando la copia ocurre entre dos destinos remotos.

internal-sftp in sshd in OpenSSH before 10.4 recognizes only the first 9 command-line arguments, which can be important if a later command-line argument would have helped to ensure the intended security properties of an SFTP connection.

internal-sftp en sshd en OpenSSH anterior a la versión 10.4 reconoce solo los primeros 9 argumentos de línea de comandos, lo cual puede ser importante si un argumento de línea de comandos posterior habría ayudado a garantizar las propiedades de seguridad previstas de una conexión SFTP.
sshd in OpenSSH before 10.4 has an undocumented security-relevant behavior: GSSAPIStrictAcceptorCheck has no value if the server is in Windows Active Directory.
sshd en OpenSSH antes de 10.4 tiene un comportamiento no documentado relevante para la seguridad: GSSAPIStrictAcceptorCheck no tiene valor si el servidor está en un Directorio Activo de Windows.
In sshd in OpenSSH before 10.4, DisableForwarding=yes was supposed to take precedence over PermitTunnel=yes, but did not.
En sshd en OpenSSH anterior a 10.4, se suponía que DisableForwarding=yes tenía precedencia sobre PermitTunnel=yes, pero no fue así.

sshd in OpenSSH before 10.4 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (resource consumption from excessive authentication attempts) because MaxAuthTries was mishandled for GSSAPIAuthentication.

sshd en OpenSSH anterior a 10.4 permite a atacantes remotos causar una denegación de servicio (consumo de recursos por intentos excesivos de autenticación) porque MaxAuthTries fue mal gestionado para GSSAPIAuthentication.
sshd in OpenSSH before 10.4 does not always honor the minimum authentication delay.
sshd en OpenSSH anterior a 10.4 no siempre respeta el retraso mínimo de autenticación.
ssh in OpenSSH before 10.4 can have a use-after-free when a server changes its host key during a key re-exchange. (This outcome occurs only on the client side.)

ssh en OpenSSH anterior a 10.4 puede tener un uso después de liberación cuando un servidor cambia su clave de host durante un reintercambio de claves. (Este resultado ocurre solo en el lado del cliente.)

In ssh-agent in OpenSSH before 10.5, some operations can occur remotely but were intended to occur only locally, including operations that add tokens or use keys. This is caused by misinteraction between agent locking and the session-bind@openssh.com extension.

En ssh-agent en OpenSSH anterior a 10.5, algunas operaciones pueden ocurrir remotamente pero estaban destinadas a ocurrir solo localmente, incluyendo operaciones que añaden tokens o usan claves. Esto es causado por una interacción incorrecta entre el bloqueo del agente y la extensión session-bind@openssh.com.
In ssh in OpenSSH before 10.5, a use-after-free for realloc data can occur if a certain pair of remote-forwarding operations are concurrent.
En ssh en OpenSSH anterior a 10.5, puede producirse un uso después de liberación para datos de realloc si un determinado par de operaciones de reenvío remoto son concurrentes.
In sshd in OpenSSH before 10.5, the restrict keyword (in authorized_keys) was supposed to be applicable to tunnel forwarding but was not.
En sshd en OpenSSH anterior a 10.5, la palabra clave restrict (en authorized_keys) se suponía que era aplicable al reenvío de túneles pero no lo era.
In sftp in OpenSSH before 10.6, a server can trigger directory traversal (causing files to be written to unintended locations) during a recursive copy operation.
In sshd in OpenSSH before 10.6, credentials can incorrectly persist after failure of a GSSAPIAuthentication authentication attempt.
In sshd in OpenSSH before 10.6, GSSAPIAuthentication authentication state can incorrectly be persisted across authentication attempts.
In sshd and ssh in OpenSSH before 10.6, an LZ77 dictionary coder can be used even though this is contraindicated by the arXiv 2609.07709 "Crossing the Streams" findings.

In ssh-keygen in OpenSSH before 10.6, certificates could have incorrect expiration times because of Daylight Saving mishandling. There can be a slightly more severe effect on users in certain Antarctic locations.
In sshd and ssh in OpenSSH before 10.6, there is no check for whether the maximum packet length is exceeded during decompression of highly compressed data.
In sshd in OpenSSH before 10.6, the restrict keyword (in authorized_keys) was supposed to be applicable to tunnel forwarding but was not, a different vulnerability than CVE-2026-73283.
In sshd in OpenSSH before 10.6, the value "none" for a configuration option is sometimes interpreted as a filename but was intended to mean that a feature is disabled.
In ssh in OpenSSH before 10.6, a $ or \ character can occur in a command-line username, leading to injection.
